decision_conditions: This route is relevant only if the reader has feedback in Jira that can be exported as CSV.

claim_conditions: Do not imply that the reader uses Jira; introduce the route conditionally.
Attribute the under-15-minute proof-of-concept result to the documented customer example rather than promising the same duration to the reader.

emails.user_request: Write exactly one English activation email from the Featurebase team. Reader: A product manager who just created a Featurebase workspace and wants a place to collect requests. Ask them to do one thing: Set up the first feedback board. Use a specific, documented first step and explain why it helps this reader. Keep the email under 150 words excluding subject, preview and signature. Avoid unsupported access, plan, timing and outcome claims. Use one CTA with an exact documented destination if available.
emails.job: Help a reader with existing Jira feedback decide whether to use the documented CSV-import route to begin bringing those requests into Featurebase.
emails.single_idea: If existing requests are in Jira, inspect the documented CSV-import example before deciding whether to use it as the first route into Featurebase.
emails.felt_need: I need a practical way to bring existing requests into the workspace.
emails.mechanism: A documented customer example describes importing feedback from Jira into Featurebase through CSV and having a proof of concept ready in under 15 minutes.
emails.belief_shift: Before: the reader may not know whether existing Jira feedback can be used to begin activating the workspace. After: they can inspect a documented CSV-import example and decide whether that route applies to their requests.
must_not_say: Do not claim that CSV import creates, configures, or publishes a feedback board.
Do not imply the reader uses Jira or needs to migrate from it.
Do not promise an import in under 15 minutes; that duration belongs to one customer’s proof of concept.
Do not invent a Settings path, Feedback menu, button label, required field, or direct workspace URL.
Do not claim availability on every plan or for every workspace role.
Do not introduce AI support, Help Desk, pricing, security, integrations, customer counts, or unrelated testimonials.
Do not add a second CTA or ask the reader to invite teammates, install a widget, or configure the Customer Portal.
emails.objection: Moving existing requests into a new feedback workspace may seem like a substantial setup task.
emails.tone: Direct, practical, and conditional without hype.
emails.next_step_decision: Decide whether CSV import is an appropriate way to bring the reader’s existing Jira feedback into Featurebase.
emails.next_step_value: The linked Amplemarket page provides a documented example of importing feedback from Jira into Featurebase through CSV, including that customer’s proof-of-concept experience.
emails.next_step_limit: The page documents one customer’s Jira CSV import; it does not establish the reader’s import duration, create a feedback board, document board-setup navigation, or confirm plan and role access.
emails.subject_strategy: Frame the conditional Jira-import route as a concrete activation option without implying that the reader uses Jira or promising the customer’s reported timing.
